verses.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen ones who are living as foreigners in the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, that you may obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood: Grace to you and peace be multiplied.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,
who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
Wherein you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been put to grief in various trials,
that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ —
whom not having known you love; in whom, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy unspeakable and full of glory —
receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
Concerning this salvation, the prophets sought and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that would come to you,
searching for who or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ, which was in them, pointed to, when he predicted the sufferings of Christ, and the glories that would follow them.

To them it was revealed, that not to themselves, but to you, they ministered these things, which now have been announced to you through those who preached the Good News to you by the Holy Spirit sent out from heaven; which things angels desire to look into.
Therefore prepare your minds for action,  be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ —
as children of obedience, not conforming yourselves according to your former lusts as in your ignorance,
but just as he who called you is holy, you yourselves also be holy in all of your behavior;
because it is written, “You shall be holy; for I am holy.”
If you call on him as Father, who without respect of persons judges according to each man’s work, pass the time of your living as foreigners here in reverent fear:
knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things, with silver or gold, from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers,
but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ;
who was foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in this last age for your sake,
who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead, and gave him glory; so that your faith and hope might be in God.
Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently:
having been born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, through the word of God, which lives and remains forever.
For, “All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls;
but the Lord’s word endures forever.”   This is the word of Good News which was preached to you.

footnotes.content: Peter addresses the scattered believers—foreigners in their own lands. He knows what it's like to feel homeless in the world; that's why he reminds them their Father is not far. Notice he doesn't start with guilt or duty, but with greeting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Foreknowledge, sanctification, obedience, sprinkling—every word here is rooted in covenant. Grace multiplied doesn't mean we get easier lives, but that we become more conscious of His presence in the hard ones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A living hope—not wishful thinking, but a hope born from witnessing the empty tomb. The Father's mercy didn't just save us from death; it raised us into newness while we're still breathing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice: our inheritance doesn't fade like every earthly treasure does. In a world where all we touch crumbles, this promise stands. The Lord is already holding safe what we cannot lose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Guarded by God's power—we rest in His keeping, not our own vigilance. Faith isn't the strength to hold on; it's the openness to be held until the last day.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Trials are real, and they're temporary. 'If need be'—not every season carries the same weight. Even now, in grief and difficulty, the believers' joy remains, because it rests in Someone beyond circumstance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gold perishes, but tested faith yields praise. Peter watches suffering refine us into something imperishable. When we endure by clinging to Jesus, we become proof that He is real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Loved without seeing—this is the paradox of faith. The believers know Jesus more truly by the Spirit than many who walked beside Him. Love deepens in the unseen; joy is most real when it can't be explained by the world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The result of faith is receiving—salvation isn't a doctrine to argue but a gift being worked out in your life. Peter reminds them: you're already getting what you believed for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophets diligently searched and longed to understand the grace coming to us. Peter is saying: what they reached toward, you now hold. Don't despise the grace you have; they would have given anything for it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Spirit of Christ was at work in them, pointing ahead. Even in the Old Testament, Jesus was the subject—His sufferings, His glory. The whole story converges on Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophets served a generation not their own. They were faithful stewards of mysteries they wouldn't see fulfilled. Even the angels lean in to see how grace works in human hearts—what a privilege to be the ones living it out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Prepare your minds—keep your thoughts steady on the grace that's coming, not on the sorrows here. Soberness isn't grim; it's clarity. Hope fully means don't hedge your bets with the world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We were children of disobedience in ignorance; now we're children who obey a Father we know. That's the turn—not through shame, but through sight. We obey because we've seen how good He is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Holiness isn't separation from life; it's life ordered around what is truly good and true. As He is holy, you also be—in everything you touch, every choice, every day.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A direct echo of Leviticus 11:44—God's own word, unchanged. When Peter quotes the Law, he's showing: the call to holiness is the heartbeat of all Scripture. Be who your God is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To call God Father is intimacy. To fear Him is respect. He judges fairly, no favoritism—so live as ambassadors of His name, not as fugitives. We're at home with Someone who sees and loves us completely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Redeemed—that's the word for a slave set free by payment. Your old way of life was empty inheritance from those before you. But Jesus bought you out of it. You're no longer bound to repeat their emptiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A lamb without blemish—Peter is evoking the Passover lamb, the Day of Atonement. Christ's blood isn't a symbol; it's the fulfillment of every sacrifice the old covenant pointed to. We're covered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Foreknown before the world's foundation—Christ's cross was no accident, no last-minute plan. The Father's heart toward you and toward His Son goes back beyond time itself. You were always meant to be His.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Believers in God through Christ—everything we know of the Father, we know through the Son. His resurrection and His glory make Him the hinge of all faith. Our trust and hope find their home in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Purified through obedience—not by washing ourselves clean, but by saying yes to His truth. That purifying makes us able to love one another sincerely, from the heart, without pretense.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Born again of incorruptible seed—God's word, not human effort or bloodline, is what makes us new. The word that raised Jesus also raises us. That seed lives and lasts forever in us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Quoting Isaiah 40:6—the prophet knows all earthly glory is transient. Grass and flowers were the preachers' way of saying: don't put your hope in what will fade. A humbling, true word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this: amid all that changes—fashions, fortunes, nations rising and falling—the Lord's word endures. The good news preached to them, to us, stands firm. Everything else is dust; His word remains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
